Partial Enteral Nutrition (PEN)
The limited tolerability of EEN led to the trial of approaches to improve adherence to therapy. Partial Enteral Nutrition (PEN) is
a diet that combines EEN with an unrestricted oral diet. Unfortunately, PEN does not seem to be as effective in treating active disease
as EEN. In an observational study of 90 children with active CD who were allocated to PEN with unrestricted diet, EEN or anti-TNF
at the clinician’s discretion, fecal calprotectin reductions to <250 mg/g and rates of clinical response were measured by Pediatric
disease indices. A fecal calprotectin level of 250 mg/g was selected as an appropriate cutoff as this has previously been shown to
correlate well with endoscopic remission in CD (D’Haens et al., 2012). The improvements in these parameters were less in the
PEN group compared to those receiving EEN and anti-TNF therapy (FC to <250 PEN 14%, EEN 45%, anti-TNF 62%, p < 0.001,
clinical response PEN 64%, EEN 88%, anti TNF 84%, p ¼ 0.08) (Lee et al., 2015). In a randomized trial of 50 children with active
